rootCause: Java heap space exhausted — Minecraft ran out of RAM.
rootCauseDetail: Minecraft allocated all available heap memory and crashed. This usually means more RAM is needed, or a mod is leaking memory.
technicalDetail: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space — the JVM ran out of heap memory during execution.
evidenceTemplates: OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space detected in logs
recommendedFixes: Increase RAM allocation in Launcher Settings
Remove memory-intensive mods
Enable auto RAM allocation

rootCause: Process killed by the Android OS due to insufficient system RAM (exit code 137).
rootCauseDetail: Android's low-memory killer terminated Minecraft because the device ran out of available RAM. This is common on devices with 3 GB RAM or less.
technicalDetail: Exit code 137 = SIGKILL sent by the Android OOM killer. The process did not crash — it was forcibly terminated.
evidenceTemplates: Exit code 137 — OOM-killed by Android OS
recommendedFixes: Reduce RAM allocation to avoid triggering the OOM killer
Close background apps before launching
Remove mods that consume excessive memory

rootCause: Renderer caused a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) — native renderer library crashed.
rootCauseDetail: The graphics renderer crashed with a fatal memory error. This is almost always caused by an incompatibility between the selected renderer and your GPU driver.
technicalDetail: SIGSEGV in a renderer or GL library. Exit code 139 or signal 11.
evidenceTemplates: SIGSEGV (segmentation fault) detected — renderer native crash
libEGL reference found in crash context
recommendedFixes: Switch to a different renderer (e.g., from ANGLE to MobileGlues)
Reset renderer settings to defaults
Check GPU compatibility database for your device

rootCause: EGL (OpenGL ES) context creation failed — renderer cannot initialize.
rootCauseDetail: The renderer failed to create an EGL context. This means OpenGL ES is not working on your device with the current renderer. Try switching to a different renderer.
technicalDetail: EGL context creation failure — eglCreateContext or eglMakeCurrent returned an error.
recommendedFixes: Switch to a different renderer
Reset renderer configuration

rootCause: A mod dependency is missing — required class not found.
rootCauseDetail: A mod is trying to use a class from another mod or library that isn't installed. Make sure all required dependencies are installed and that their versions match.
technicalDetail: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError or ClassNotFoundException — a class required by an installed mod could not be found at runtime.
evidenceTemplates: NoClassDefFoundError — required class missing at runtime
ClassNotFoundException — class not found in classpath
recommendedFixes: Install missing mod dependencies
Update all mods to versions compatible with each other
Check mod documentation for required dependencies

rootCause: A mod is calling a method that no longer exists — API version mismatch.
rootCauseDetail: A mod was built against a different version of another mod or Minecraft's API. This usually happens when mods are not updated together, or when mixing mods from different Minecraft versions.
technicalDetail: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError — a method signature has changed between the version the mod was compiled against and the version currently installed.
recommendedFixes: Update Fabric API to the latest version
Update the conflicting mod
Remove incompatible mods
Verify all mods target the same Minecraft version

rootCauseDetail: Fabric Loader found that one or more of your mods are incompatible with each other or with the current Minecraft version. Check the error message for the specific conflicting mod.
technicalDetail: net.fabricmc.loader reported 'Incompatible mod set' — a dependency constraint was violated.
evidenceTemplates: Fabric Loader class found in crash context
recommendedFixes: Read the Fabric error message to identify conflicting mods
Update or remove the incompatible mod
Ensure Fabric API version matches the mods' requirements

rootCauseDetail: Two or more mods are both trying to modify the same part of Minecraft's code using Mixin, and their changes are incompatible. This is a known issue when combining certain mods.
technicalDetail: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.MixinException or 'Cannot apply mixin' — Mixin injection failed due to conflicting modifications.
evidenceTemplates: SpongePowered ASM Mixin framework reference found
recommendedFixes: Identify conflicting mods from the Mixin error message
Remove or disable one of the conflicting mods
Check if there is a compatibility patch mod available

rootCause: Java class file version mismatch — wrong Java version is installed.
rootCauseDetail: Minecraft (or a mod) was compiled for a newer version of Java than you have installed. For example, Minecraft 1.17+ requires Java 17 or later, but Java 8 was detected.
technicalDetail: java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError — the class file version is higher than the version supported by the installed JVM.
evidenceTemplates: Unsupported class file major version — Java version mismatch
recommendedFixes: Install Java 17 or later for Minecraft 1.17+
Install Java 21 for Minecraft 1.21+
Select the correct Java runtime in Launcher Settings

rootCause: An invalid or unrecognized JVM argument prevented the JVM from starting.
rootCauseDetail: One of the JVM arguments you have set is not supported by the installed Java version, or has been misspelled. The JVM exits immediately when it encounters an unrecognized argument.
technicalDetail: JVM startup failure due to unrecognized flag — the JVM printed an error about an unrecognized VM option.

patterns.value: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine

evidenceTemplates: JVM creation failure — possibly caused by bad JVM arguments
recommendedFixes: Reset JVM arguments to safe defaults
Remove deprecated flags like -XX:+AggressiveOpts

rootCause: Sodium and OptiFine are both installed — these mods are incompatible.
rootCauseDetail: Sodium and OptiFine both replace Minecraft's rendering engine and cannot be used together. Remove OptiFine and use Iris for shader support instead.
technicalDetail: Known incompatible mod pair: Sodium + OptiFine. These mods replace overlapping rendering systems.
evidenceTemplates: OptiFine detected in logs — known conflict with Sodium
recommendedFixes: Remove OptiFine from your mods folder
Use Iris Shaders instead of OptiFine for shader support
Keep Sodium installed as a performance mod

rootCauseDetail: A native library called abort() or triggered an assertion failure. This is often caused by a renderer library, GPU driver, or corrupted native dependency.
technicalDetail: Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT) — process abort. Check hs_err_pid log for the crashing frame.
evidenceTemplates: SIGABRT signal detected — native library abort
recommendedFixes: Switch to a different renderer
Reinstall the Java runtime
Check for GPU driver updates

rootCause: World data appears corrupted — level.dat or chunk data is unreadable.
rootCauseDetail: Minecraft encountered corrupted world data while loading or during play. This can happen after a crash, storage failure, or interrupted save.
technicalDetail: IOException or NBT parsing failure while reading level.dat or chunk region files.
evidenceTemplates: level.dat reference found in crash context
recommendedFixes: Restore the world from a backup if available
Try loading a different world to verify the issue is world-specific
Use a world repair tool

rootCause: Network connection failure during authentication or resource download.
rootCauseDetail: Minecraft could not connect to Mojang authentication servers or download required resources. This is usually a temporary issue — check your internet connection and try again.
technicalDetail: ConnectException, UnknownHostException, or SocketTimeoutException during network operation.
recommendedFixes: Check your internet connection
Try launching with offline mode enabled
Use a local account to bypass authentication
